name: The vārī: walking pilgrimage to Paṇḍharpūr
method_summary: Twice a year (above all for Āṣāḍhī ekādaśī, again for Kārtikī) Vārkarīs walk to Paṇḍharpūr in singing companies (diṇḍī) behind the palanquins bearing the sandals of Jñāneśvar from Āḷandī and Tukārām from Dehu, singing abhaṅgas and the name by day, holding kīrtan and bhajan at the halts, keeping the ekādaśī fast, bathing in the Candrabhāgā and taking darśan of Viṭṭhala (or of the temple's pinnacle when the crowds are too great). Those who keep it for life are Vārkarīs.
prerequisites: wearing the tuḷsī necklace (for Vārkarīs proper)
vegetarian diet and abstinence on the road
duration: about three weeks on foot for the Āṣāḍhī vārī from Āḷandī/Dehu; lifelong observance
signs_of_progress: the saints' company experienced as the tīrtha
longing for Paṇḍharpūr as for a mother's home

equivalents.note: a specific, recurring, congregational pilgrimage with its own inner meaning

name: Vārkarī kīrtan
method_summary: A kīrtankār takes an abhaṅga as text and expounds it in song and speech, illustrated by the saints' lives, while a chorus with cymbals (ṭāḷ) and drum repeats the refrain and the name ('Jñānobā Tukārām', 'Rāma Kṛṣṇa Hari'); it ends with the name and the Pasāydān. Nāmdev is remembered as its founder.

name: Congregational song (bhajan)
method_summary: Groups sing abhaṅgas, padas or dohās and the name together with cymbals and drum, in the evening, at festivals and on the road; in the Vārkarī form a leader sings and the group answers.

name: Week of the name (harināma saptāh)
method_summary: A village holds seven days of continuous singing of the name and reading of the Jñāneśvarī or the Gāthā, with nightly kīrtan, ending with a common meal.

name: Taking the tuḷsī necklace (Vārkarī initiation)
method_summary: A senior Vārkarī places the tuḷsī-bead necklace (māḷ) on the new member, who vows to keep the vārī, to be vegetarian and abstain from intoxicants, to observe ekādaśī and to remember the name.

name: Recitation of the tradition's scripture (pārāyaṇa)
method_summary: Reading or chanting a whole scripture in a set period: the Jñāneśvarī or Gāthā (Vārkarī), the Rāmcaritmānas in nine days (navāhna) or a month (māsa-pārāyaṇa) (Rāmānandī and wider Hindi-speaking devotion), the Kīrtana-ghoṣā and Bhāgavata in the nāmghar (Ekaśaraṇa).

name: The 'royal road' of kuṇḍalinī in the Jñāneśvarī
method_summary: Summary only: Jñāneśvar's commentary on the Gītā's seated meditation describes posture and bodily locks waking kuṇḍalinī, her rise through the centres and merging in the supreme at the crown. No steps, holds or durations are recorded here.
prerequisites: the Gītā's conditions for meditation: a clean, steady seat, a restrained mind and senses (BhG 6.10–14), which Jñāneśvar expands
the guru's grace in the Nāth line (Jñāneśvarī 18)

warnings.text: The text's own cautions are not recorded at this skeleton stage; to be extracted from Jñāneśvarī 6 (see REPORT gaps).

name: Repetition of Rāma's name and mantra
method_summary: Repeating the Rāma mantra received at initiation (Rāmānandī: the six-syllable mantra) or the name 'Rāma' aloud, softly or mentally, often on tulsī beads; the Samartha sampradāya uses the thirteen-syllable 'śrī rām jay rām jay jay rām'; tradition credits Samartha Rāmdās with thirteen crore repetitions at Ṭākaḷī.

equivalents.note: the same practice with Rāma's name/mantra

name: Rāmlīlā (enactment of the Rāma story)
method_summary: The Rāmcaritmānas is recited while its episodes are enacted over many nights, above all at Navarātri–Daśaharā; the boy-actors playing Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa are honoured as the deities during the performance. Tradition links its beginning at Vārāṇasī to Tulsīdās and his circle.

name: Worship of Hanumān
method_summary: Recitation of the Hanumān Cālīsā (often on Tuesdays and Saturdays) and worship at Hanumān/Māruti shrines as Rāma's servant and remover of obstacles; the Samartha sampradāya joins it to the cultivation of bodily strength.

name: Worship in the grove (nikuñja-upāsanā)
method_summary: The devotee, as a sakhī, contemplates and inwardly serves the eternal pair at play in the grove through the founders' songs, temple service and meditation on the daily round of their play; no personal union is sought.

equivalents.note: Nimbārkī worship of the divine couple; the Haridāsī/Rādhāvallabha forms stress the grove and the sakhī stance

name: Collective temple singing (samāj-gāyan)
method_summary: Temple musicians and devotees sing the founders' padas in fixed rāgas and style before the deity at set times.

name: The Mahānubhāva renunciant discipline
method_summary: Monks and nuns keep moving (aṭana), live by begging, keep no possessions, harm no creature, avoid worldly company and remain in remembrance of Parameśvara and his incarnations.

name: Remembering the incarnations' deeds
method_summary: Reading, reciting and meditating on the episodes of the Līḷācaritra and the lives of the five Kṛṣṇas as the devotee's constant remembrance.

name: Veneration of sanctified places
method_summary: Visiting and worshipping at places the incarnations visited and venerating objects associated with them.

name: Congregational worship of the name (nām-prasaṅga)
method_summary: In the nāmghar, before the book on the guru-āsana, a leader sings verses of the Kīrtana-ghoṣā and Nām-ghoṣā and the congregation responds with the name, with cymbals and drum, at set times of day and on festivals.

name: Taking refuge (śaraṇ)
method_summary: Initiation by a sattrādhikār: the disciple takes refuge in the four real things — the name, Kṛṣṇa, the guru and the devotees — and vows exclusive devotion; open to all castes and peoples.

name: Devotional drama (bhāonā)
method_summary: An aṅkīyā nāṭ is staged in the nāmghar with the sūtradhāra singing and dancing, masks, music and song; performing and watching are acts of worship.

name: Singing bargīts
method_summary: The rāga songs of Śaṅkaradeva and Mādhavadeva are sung, often at dawn and at the opening of sattra services, with prescribed rāga and tāla.

name: Worship through music (nādopāsana)
method_summary: Singing the Lord's praise in rāga as worship, with devotion as its condition (Tyāgarāja); in Vṛndāvana, dhrupad singing of the pair's play (Svāmī Haridās).

name: Service to one's parents
method_summary: Serving one's parents as worship: Puṇḍalīka's service was so pleasing that the Lord waited on a brick.

name: Devotional singing (kīrtana)
method_summary: Vārkarī: kīrtan and bhajan on abhaṅgas with the name; Ekaśaraṇa: kīrtana from the Kīrtana-ghoṣā, with hearing the foremost of devotions; Rāmānandī: singing Rāma's qualities, which in Kali carries one across.

name: Congregational chanting of the name (nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Vārkarī: the easy means that burns the sins of many births and brings the Lord home; Ekaśaraṇa: the name sung together in the nāmghar.

name: Repetition of the divine name on beads (nāma-japa)
method_summary: Vārkarī: 'Rāma Kṛṣṇa Hari' on the tuḷsī necklace; Haridāsī: constant remembrance of Hari's name, since death is near.

name: Holy company (satsaṅga)
method_summary: Seeking and serving the company of saints: without it no discernment (Tulsī); asked above liberation (Tukārām); Mīrā sat with sādhus against her family; Tyāgarāja salutes all great souls.

name: Ekādaśī fast
method_summary: Vārkarīs fast on every ekādaśī, and the Āṣāḍhī and Kārtikī ekādaśīs are the goal of the vārī.

name: The nine forms of devotion (navadhā bhakti)
method_summary: Rāmānandī: Tulsī's nine to Śabarī, any one sufficing; Rāmdāsī: the Bhāgavata's nine expounded in Dāsbodh 4; Ekaśaraṇa: hearing and singing foremost.

name: Recitation of the Rāma tāraka mantra
method_summary: Rāmānandī reading: Śiva liberates those dying at Kāśī by the power of Rāma's name.

name: Pilgrimage to tīrthas
method_summary: Vārkarī: pilgrimage is valued, but the saints' company and Viṭṭhala's feet are the true tīrtha (Nāmdev's Tīrthāvaḷī).

name: Recitation of the tradition's hymns
method_summary: Rāmānandī and wider north Indian practice: daily recitation of the Hanumān Cālīsā and passages of the Mānas.

name: Taking refuge in the Lord (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Rāmānandī: turning one's face to Rāma, who never abandons one who comes for refuge (Vibhīṣaṇa); Haridāsī: living as Hari keeps one; Ekaśaraṇa: single refuge in Kṛṣṇa.

name: The eightfold daily service (aṣṭayāma sevā)
method_summary: Rādhāvallabha temples serve Rādhāvallabha through the eight periods of the day, with the sakhīs' songs appropriate to each (as recalled; details to verify).

name: Worship of the divine couple (yugala-upāsanā)
method_summary: In the Rādhāvallabha and Haridāsī traditions the pair are worshipped together as inseparable, Rādhā supreme (Rādhāvallabha) or the natural pair in the grove (Haridāsī).

name: Meditation on the deity's form
method_summary: Vārkarī: meditation on Viṭṭhala's form standing on the brick, hands on hips, tuḷsī garland at the neck.
